scope: Theorem 5.1 (Rank-one gradient and Hessian estimates) of the manuscript “The nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality and original-data rigidity” (preprints/The-nonmaximal-anti-de-Sitter-Penrose-Inequality-and-original-data-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e2b9ba2768918dc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let U be an interior coordinate ball or a smooth boundary half-ball, with a uniformly controlled C2 metric g. In the boundary case use Gaussian coordinates, so g33 = 1 and ga3 = 0 for a = 1, 2. Suppose that z is smooth on U, up to the face on its original side in the boundary case, and satisfies Aij ∇i∇jz = G, Aij = gij − (1 − b)ei ej , e = ∇z |∇z| , c0 ≤ b ≤ 1, (5.1) where c0 > 0. In the boundary case assume that z is constant on the face. At a zero of ∇z, an arbitrary measurable unit direction is allowed, provided Equation (5.1) holds with that choice. Assume |∇z| ≤ L and |G| ≤ Q. There are α ∈ (0, 1), a uniform positive radius r0, and C, depending only on c0, the indicated geometry, and separation from the other faces of the patch, such that on a smaller patch ∥Dz∥C0,α ≤ C(L + Q), ˆ Br(x)∩U | Hess z|2 dVg ≤ C(L + Q)2 r1+2α (0 < r ≤ r0). (5.2) The constants α, r0, C do not depend on a modulus of continuity of b or G. The same assertion holds for uniformly controlled families of patches.
